## Diffusion face coefficient at a wall: one-sided extrapolation instead of the ghost (automatic) {#sec-ch09-wallcoef}

### Summary

A reflecting wall fills its ghost cells with the mirror image of the interior. That is the right state for the
Riemann solver, but the average of a cell and its mirror is the cell's own value, half a cell away from the wall,
so the face coefficient of a stratified column is off by a factor $e^{\mp h/2H}$ at the walls, an $O(h)$ error.
The diffusion module therefore extrapolates the coefficient from the two interior cells next to the wall, which
reads no ghost at all and is exact for a linear profile.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** On an $x_1$ face that is a reflecting wall, takes the diffusion coefficient by linear extrapolation
from the two nearest interior cells instead of averaging the wall cell with its ghost;
@eq-ch09-wallcoef-extrap.

**Data.** In: the two nearest cell coefficients and widths; out: the wall-face diffusion coefficient.

**Placement.** Inside the diffusion module, wherever it forms a face coefficient, every stage.

**Activation.** No switch: automatic when the $x_1$ boundary function is named `reflecting_inner`/`_outer` or
`fixed_temperature_inner`/`_outer`. Every other face keeps the two-cell average.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact for a linear coefficient, second order otherwise; falls back to the wall cell's value
if the extrapolation is not positive; needs two interior $x_1$ cells.

**Evidence.** Report checks and source-test assertions are listed below; solver ctests were not run at the pin.
:::

**Data details.** In: the coefficient ($\rho$ or $\rho c_v$, either times an $x_1$ profile) of the wall cell and its
interior neighbour, cell averages, and their $x_1$ widths; the recorded name of the $x_1$ boundary function. Out: the
coefficient on the wall face. Check cases: 100 random stretched columns with a linear coefficient, and
$\rho=\rho_0e^{-x_1/H}$ at $h/H$ from $1/32$ to $1/64$.

**Evidence details.** Tests: on a linear density a uniform $\mathrm{d}T/\mathrm{d}n$ gives the same tendency in every interior cell,
{{< code tests/test_diffusion.cpp DeviceTest.wall_face_coefficient_reads_no_ghost >}} ($10^{-5}$); the wall flux does
not depend on the ghost density,
{{< code tests/test_diffusion.cpp DeviceTest.wall_flux_does_not_depend_on_the_ghost_density >}} ($10^{-10}$); only the
four names count, {{< code tests/test_diffusion.cpp diffusion_options.wall_names_are_an_exact_whitelist >}} (exact);
these ctests were not run at the pin. Check: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/checks/wallcoef_check.py`, output `wallcoef_check.out` lines `[C1]`–`[C5]`, re-run at the pin: all PASS, output identical [^env-wallcoef].

Local symbols: cells $0$ and $1$ the wall cell and its interior neighbour; $h_0$, $h_1$ [m]
their $x_1$ widths; $q$ the cell field whose face value is taken ($\rho$ or $\rho c_v$, either times an $x_1$ profile); $q_f$ its
value on the wall face; $\alpha_{\mathrm f}=h_0/(h_0+h_1)$ [-] the extrapolation weight (code `t`; $t$ is time in appendix A),
the same weight as @sec-ch09-relax's at-face target; $H$[^rg-9cd2e19a185e] [m] the scale height of the check's profile. $h$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$
are defined in @sec-appa.

The rule is restricted to $x_1$ and to a list of boundary names. An $x_2$ or $x_3$ reflecting face is as likely to
be a symmetry plane, where the mirror is exact and the average is the better estimate; and `reflecting` is the
default for every face a configuration does not name, so a wider rule would change runs that did not ask for it.
Periodic, outflow, custom and solid boundary functions keep the average.

### Derivation

Let cell $0$ touch the wall and cell $1$ be its interior neighbour, with widths $h_0$, $h_1$. The wall face is
$h_0/2$ from the centre of cell $0$ and the two centres are $(h_0+h_1)/2$ apart, so the linear interpolant through
the two centre values, evaluated at the face, is

$$
\begin{aligned}
q_f &= (1+\alpha_{\mathrm f})\,q_0 - \alpha_{\mathrm f}\,q_1, \\
\alpha_{\mathrm f} &= \frac{h_0}{h_0+h_1},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-wallcoef-extrap}

<!-- equation-check: eq-ch09-wallcoef-extrap ch09_dropin_check.py [D3b] -->

the same expression at both walls, because the offset to the face and the direction to the second cell change
sign together. @eq-ch09-wallcoef-extrap is `extrapolate_to_wall`
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp extrapolate_to_wall >}}). Why it is exact for a linear $q$, in three steps.

1. *The line through the two centres* has slope $(q_0-q_1)/[(h_0+h_1)/2]$ toward the wall.
2. *The wall face* is $h_0/2$ from the centre of cell 0, so $q_f=q_0+\tfrac{h_0}{2}\cdot\tfrac{2(q_0-q_1)}{h_0+h_1}
   =(1+\alpha_{\mathrm f})q_0-\alpha_{\mathrm f}q_1$, @eq-ch09-wallcoef-extrap, with no assumption on $h_0$, $h_1$.
3. *Hence* it is exact for a linear $q$ on any widths, and, by Taylor's theorem, second order for a smooth one.

*Round-off.* `t` is one addition and one division, $\hat\alpha_{\mathrm f}=\alpha_{\mathrm f}(1+\eta_\alpha)$ with $\lvert\eta_\alpha\rvert\le2\cdot\tfrac{\epsilon_{\mathrm m}}2$,
and `(1. + t) * vnear - t * vnext` adds four roundings, so to first order

$$
\lvert\hat q_f-q_f\rvert\le\tfrac{\epsilon_{\mathrm m}}2\big[2\alpha_{\mathrm f}\lvert q_0-q_1\rvert+2(1+\alpha_{\mathrm f})\lvert q_0\rvert+\alpha_{\mathrm f}\lvert q_1\rvert+\lvert q_f\rvert\big]
$$

(check: at most 0.761 of it), consistent with $8.9\times10^{-16}$ relative over 100 random stretched columns.[^wall-c]
If $q_f\le0$ the code returns $q_0$, which also reads no ghost (`[C3]`).

The mirror average, by contrast, returns $q_0$ itself. For $\rho=\rho_0e^{-x_1/H}$ with the lower wall at $x_1=0$
the ratio of the mirror average to the wall value is exactly $e^{-h/2H}$ at the lower wall and $e^{+h/2H}$ at the
upper one, an $O(h)$ error; the extrapolation error falls at second order (`[C2]`: fitted orders 0.994 and 1.985
for $h/H$ from $1/32$ to $1/64$).

Which fluxes the coefficient matters for follows from the mirror parities. Density and temperature are mirrored
even, so the face-normal temperature difference at a reflecting wall is exactly zero and the conductive wall flux
vanishes whatever the coefficient. The normal velocity is mirrored odd, so $\partial_1v_1 = 2v_{1,0}/h_0$ at the
wall (`[C4]`), and the viscous normal stress at the wall carries the coefficient. At a reflecting wall the rule
therefore changes the viscous wall flux, and nothing else.

*Exact and truncated.* The coefficient is exact for linear profiles and $O(h^2)$ otherwise; the normal-stress
kernel at the wall stays $O(h)$ (@sec-ch09-viscosity, Limits).

[^wall-c]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/checks/wallcoef_check.py`, output `wallcoef_check.out`, lines `[C1]`–`[C5]`; a
    numpy port of `extrapolate_to_wall` and `face_coefficient` at the pin, double precision.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-wallcoef-wall compares the two estimates at the lower wall.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-wallcoef-wall
#| fig-cap: "The diffusion coefficient at a reflecting $x_1$ wall (thick black line) for $\\rho=\\rho_0e^{-x_1/H}$ with $h=H/2$, shown as $\\rho/\\rho_0$ against $x_1/H$ (both dimensionless). The blue curve is the exact profile, the sky-blue circles the two interior cell values and the hatched reddish-purple cell the mirror ghost (reddish-purple circle). Their average is the vermillion square on the wall, which equals the wall cell's value; the bluish-green dashed line is the extrapolation from the two interior cells, which lands on the bluish-green diamond near the exact wall value."
#| fig-alt: "Plot of an exponential density near a wall, with a hatched ghost cell to the left of the wall, two interior cell values, the mirror-average point on the wall below the curve and the extrapolated point on the wall close to the curve."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.figures.fig_wallcoef_wall import make_fig
make_fig()
```

`face_coefficient` applies the extrapolation to the first and last $x_1$ face of a block when that face is a listed
wall and the block has at least three $x_1$ faces, that is two interior cells; with fewer the average is kept
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp face_coefficient >}}). A seam between two blocks has no boundary function and so
is never a wall. The same rule applies to the product of a coefficient and an $x_1$ profile, which is extrapolated
as one quantity (@sec-ch09-x1profile). It runs wherever the module computes a coefficient, in every stage.

### Code

**A minimal input.** The rule has no key; it fires when a named reflecting function is installed on an $x_1$ face:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `boundary-condition`[^rg-804a8ad5a6ca], `external`[^rg-dd0c9c96e778], `x1-inner`[^rg-e47c63c1416e], `x1-outer`[^rg-8044641eea15].
```yaml
boundary-condition:
  external:
    x1-inner: reflecting   # recorded as reflecting_inner: the wall face is extrapolated
    x1-outer: reflecting
forcing:
  diffusion: {nu_iso: 0.5, kappa_iso: 0.25}
```

**What is refused, and why.** Nothing: the rule is a choice inside `face_coefficient`. A boundary function installed
with no recorded name is not refused but warned about once ("a boundary function is installed with no recorded name,
so it cannot be classified as a wall …", {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp >}}), and the average is kept there.

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch09-wallcoef-extrap** (`extrapolate_to_wall` and `face_coefficient`):

```cpp
auto t = wnear / (wnear + wnext);
...
auto wall = (1. + t) * vnear - t * vnext;
return torch::where(wall > 0., wall, vnear);
...
if (nface < 3) return out;  // fewer than two active cells to extrapolate from
```

`wnear`, `wnext` are $h_0$, $h_1$ and `t` is $\alpha_{\mathrm f}$; `wall` is $q_f$, replaced by $q_0$ (`vnear`) when not positive; the last
line keeps the two-cell average on a block with fewer than two interior $x_1$ cells.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| @eq-ch09-wallcoef-extrap and the fallback | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp extrapolate_to_wall >}} | `extrapolate_to_wall` | |
| average, or wall faces | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp face_coefficient >}} | `face_coefficient` | |
| $x_1$ only | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward >}} | `is_wall_boundary` | $x_1$ faces |
| the list of wall names | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_wall_boundary >}} | `is_wall_boundary` | boundary names |
| unnamed function warns | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_wall_boundary >}} | `TORCH_WARN_ONCE` | |
| installed-function test | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_physical_boundary >}} | `is_physical_boundary` | |

: Code map of the wall face coefficient. {#tbl-ch09-wallcoef-code}

1. For each active direction `DiffusionImpl::forward` asks `is_wall_boundary` about the lower and upper $x_1$ face
   only ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward >}}).
2. `is_wall_boundary` returns true for an installed function whose recorded name is one of the four wall names
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_wall_boundary >}}); a function with no recorded
   name warns once with `TORCH_WARN_ONCE` and returns false.
3. `face_coefficient` averages every face and overwrites the wall faces with `extrapolate_to_wall`
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp face_coefficient >}}, {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp extrapolate_to_wall >}}).

::: {.callout-important title="Check"}
**Evidence.** The check numbers come from the port named in the footnote. The error of the mirror average through
the solver on a stratified column is **not measured at the pin**: no committed deck runs it. ctest cases:
**pending a pinned ctest run**.
**Coverage.** CPU float32/float64 and CUDA when present for the `DeviceTest` cases; no multi-rank test. A
stretched $x_1$ (`geometry/x1f` or `cells/x1rat`) gives the general weight $\alpha_{\mathrm f}\ne\tfrac12$; no Cartesian ctest
runs it, so on the Cartesian grid it is covered only by `[C1]` here and `[C3]` of `stretched_x1_check.py`
(@sec-ch09-viscosity). The same weight on the cubed-sphere radial walls is tested by
`stretched_radial_implicit_wall_k` (@sec-ch09-csdiffusion).
:::

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Without a `boundary-condition.external` block no boundary functions exist and the rule never fires. Immersed
solids are read as fluid by the diffusion module, with a face heat capacity about 500 times too large.
:::

1. **Immersed solids.** The solid placeholder state, $\rho=10^3$ and $p=10^9$ by default
   ({{< code src/bc/internal_boundary.hpp InternalBoundaryOptionsImpl >}}), is written into $\mathbf W$ by
   `mark_prim_solid_` before the forcings run ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). A fluid
   face next to a solid then has $\rho c_v$ 500.5 times the fluid value and a temperature jump of a factor 10
   (`[C5]`). The energy this deposits in the cells beside a solid is **not measured at the pin**. No deck in
   `examples/` or `tests/` combines a solid mask with diffusion. Not tested.
2. **Dormant without named boundaries.** No boundary block, or a function installed from Python with no `name`[^rg-8f699befd93b],
   means no wall: the average is used, with a one-time warning in the second case.
3. **`fixed_temperature_*`** is on the list, but no boundary function of that name is registered in `src/` at the
   pin, so that entry changes nothing.
4. **Positivity fallback** is element-wise and silent; a wall face can be second order in some columns and first
   order in others. Not observed to fire; not measured.
5. **Block too short.** With fewer than two interior $x_1$ cells, `nface` $<3$, the average is kept
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp face_coefficient >}}).
